Manage high-stakes relationships with external tax, legal, and audit partners to mitigate risk and defend the organization’s fiscal standing.

The Senior Finance Partner maintains the following recurring governance schedule to address variances and align on strategic pivots.

jobs.description: Amazon Customer Service supports customers around the world through one of the world’s largest and most diverse customer service workforces. As AI fundamentally changes how customer service work is performed, it also creates an opportunity to reinvent how associates learn, develop their capabilities, receive coaching, and continuously improve. The Associate Development team is building the next generation of learning, coaching and performance experiences for Amazon Customer Service Associates. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build these systems from the ground up. This is a highly greenfield opportunity. Rather than digitizing traditional training and coaching processes, we are rethinking how associate development should work in an AI-native world. What does an associate need to learn before doing a job? What can they learn through experience? What should AI provide in the flow of work? How can we understand an associate’s evolving capabilities and use that understanding to personalize development? How can generative AI help provide timely, relevant and effective coaching at the scale of a global workforce? Imagine systems that continuously learn from an associate’s experience and outcomes, identify where they would benefit from development, and deliver personalized learning or AI-powered coaching. The outcomes of those interventions can then become new evidence about the associate, creating a closed loop that gets smarter over time. As an SDE on this team, you will help define and build the technical foundations that make this possible. You will work on problems spanning generative AI, personalization, intelligent recommendations, learning and coaching systems, experimentation, data and distributed systems. You will have the opportunity to influence architecture at an early stage rather than inherit a predetermined technical solution. You will partner closely with Product, Science, UX and engineering teams across Amazon to turn ambiguous customer problems into scalable technical solutions. The systems you build have the potential to shape how Customer Service Associates around the world develop and succeed at work. This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys zero-to-one problems, emerging AI technologies, large-scale systems and building products with direct human impact. Key job responsibilities - Design and build scalable services and experiences that power personalized learning, coaching and associate development across Amazon Customer Service. - Build AI-powered coaching capabilities, including applications of generative AI that can understand context, generate relevant guidance and adapt experiences to individual associate needs. - Develop systems that connect signals about associate capability and performance with the right development intervention at the right time. - Help create closed-loop systems that measure the outcomes of learning and coaching interventions and use that evidence to continuously improve future recommendations. - Work with Product and Science partners to translate emerging models and experimentation into reliable production systems. - Make foundational architectural decisions for a greenfield product space while determining where existing Amazon capabilities can be reused or evolved. - Design APIs, data models and integration patterns that allow Associate Development capabilities to interact with associate context, workflow and other Customer Service systems. - Build mechanisms for experimentation, measurement and observability so we can understand whether the experiences we create actually improve associate and customer outcomes. - Deliver secure, reliable and globally scalable systems while maintaining a high bar for operational excellence. A day in the life You might start the day working with a scientist on how an AI coaching experience can use an associate’s recent performance context to generate more useful coaching. Later, you could whiteboard an architecture for measuring whether that coaching actually changed future performance, review an API contract with another CS platform team, and prototype a new generative-AI capability. Because the space is early, you won’t simply be executing against a fully specified roadmap. You will help answer fundamental technical questions, prototype alternatives, make architecture decisions, and turn successful experiments into production systems capable of serving associates globally. About the team The Associate Experience (AE) team is building the future of work for Amazon Customer Service Associates. Our vision is to create a trusted Customer Service experience by enabling associates to succeed as the role evolves toward complex and non-deterministic problem solving. Within AE, the Associate Development team is reinventing how associates learn, develop and improve, moving beyond one-size-fits-all training and coaching towards, personalized development powered by AI. Engineers joining the team will shape foundational architecture, drive technology choices, and build AI-powered products from the ground up for one of the world's largest customer service workforces.

jobs.description: About the Role We are seeking a hands-on Infrastructure Engineer to build and automate modern enterprise infrastructure platforms. This is an engineering-first role focused on automation, platform build, and scalable system delivery. You will work within an established architecture to deliver infrastructure through code, not operate it through tickets. Just as important, you will understand the platforms you are automating: the hypervisor, the operating system, and the storage beneath them, well enough to engineer them deliberately and to debug them when the runbook runs out. What You'll D o · Build and deploy infrastructure platforms across VMware and/or Nutanix, and Windows and Linux environments · Develop and implement Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions · Automate manual processes through scripting and pipelines · Contribute to infrastructure lifecycle activities: deployment, upgrades, scaling, capacity, and optimization · Support and build Kubernetes and container environments · Troubleshoot production issues below the level of the tooling, across the hypervisor, operating system, storage, and network, and drive them to root cause · Create and maintain engineering documentation: runbooks, LLDs, and handoff materials Requirements · 3-5 years of hands-on infrastructure or systems engineering · Fluent in both written and spoken English language · Experience building and deploying production infrastructure environments · Demonstrable depth in at least one core infrastructure domain, whether virtualization, operating systems, or storage, beyond the tools used to automate it Technical Requirements Strong hands-on experience with: · VMware or Nutanix. You have built, upgraded, and sized clusters, not only consumed virtual machines from them. · Windows or Linux as an engineered platform. You have hardened, tuned, patched, and troubleshot it, not only logged into it. · Terraform and/or Ansible. You have personally built infrastructure using these tools. · PowerShell, Python, or Bash Working experience with: · Kubernetes or another container platform. You have deployed workloads, configured namespaces and RBAC, and troubleshot a cluster you did not personally stand up. Familiarity with: · Storage, backup, or disaster recovery, including provisioning, data protection, and recovery validation. Must-Have Capabilities You must be able to clearly demonstrate: · You have personally built and deployed infrastructure, not just supported it · You have automated repetitive work using code or pipelines · You have worked in code-driven environments (Git, CI/CD) · You can clearly explain what you built vs. what your team owned · You can explain what runs beneath the tooling. Expect to be asked how a container is actually isolated, why a virtual machine is slow when the host is not busy, or where a write goes between the application and the disk. Fluency with Terraform, Helm, or a CI/CD pipeline does not answer these questions on its own. What This Role Is NOT · Not a ticket-driven role. You will not be measured on queue volume. · Not a senior-level architecture or platform ownership role We do not screen out operations-titled experience. Deep infrastructure knowledge is most often earned running production systems, and that background is welcome here. What matters is what you understand and what you have personally built. Multiple-choice fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900, AWS Cloud Practitioner, or Terraform Associate do not substitute. · Experience building or supporting Kubernetes environments at production scale · Experience creating reusable automation or IaC components · Performance tuning, capacity work, or a root-cause investigation you can walk through end to end How You'll Be Successful / Bottom Line You think like an engineer, not an operator, solving infrastructure challenges through code, automating manual work, and building scalable, repeatable systems. You take ownership of what you deliver and can clearly demonstrate what you've built and automated in production. You also understand how the platforms underneath your automation actually work, because provisioning a system you cannot explain is not engineering. This role is for engineers who build infrastructure through code, automate everything possible, and can account for every layer of what they deliver. jobs.description: About the team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) org sits at the intersection of product, engineering, research, and go-to-market. We take frontier platform capabilities into the real world with design partners, turning raw customer signal into shipped software, repeatable patterns, and durable products. The FDE Platform team is primarily a leverage function that scales the FDE org’s impact to OpenAI’s platform and products. We provide hands-on leverage by embedding with customer-tagged FDE pods to aid in architecting, product shaping, refactoring, and building. This team is perfect for highly collaborative software engineers who love innovating on cutting-edge products with other builders. About the role As the Engineering Manager for Platform FDE, you will lead a small team that acts as a multiplier for the broader FDE org. Your mandate is to increase the rate at which customer-grounded ideas become durable, generalizable platform bets, by providing hands-on product and engineering leverage to customer-tagged pods. You will partner with customer-tagged FDEs who are driving delivery and customer outcomes, and embed Platform FDE capacity where they can provide the highest leverage. In practice that means working in the trenches on architecture, product shaping, refactoring, hardening, and reusable abstractions, while preserving the pod’s ownership of customer understanding and day-to-day execution. You will also collaborate closely with our B2B Platform Team and other long-term owners to align early on what should generalize, what should remain customer-specific, and what “ready for handoff” looks like. This role requires a combination of engineering leadership and strong product-oriented judgment. You will manage a focused portfolio of platform incubation work with explicit hypotheses, success criteria, and measurable adoption outcomes, and you will be accountable for translating deployment signal into reusable capabilities that can be handed off cleanly to long-term owners. You will be expected to lead through influence across multiple stakeholders, uphold a high technical bar, and establish clear responsibility boundaries between your team, customer pods, and partner organizations. This role is based in San Francisco and is not a travel role. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel is optional-by-project and typically <10%, with occasional spikes for key embeds or launches. In this role you will - Guide a focused portfolio of platform bets: Steer direction for a small number of high-signal problems, with clear hypotheses, success criteria, sequencing, and measurable adoption outcomes. - Build and validate with customers: Ensure the team ships working software with design partners, instruments usage and outcomes, and iterates quickly based on real-world adoption and constraints. - Co-develop with long-term owners: Partner early with B2B Platform (and other durable owners) to align on architecture, interfaces, security/governance requirements, and handoff criteria, staying engaged through validation and the path to scale. - Maintain a high engineering bar: Set and enforce standards for design, code quality, testing, observability, and operational readiness appropriate for enterprise use. - Grow and develop the team: Coach and develop engineers through direct feedback, clear expectations, and durable team mechanisms that reinforce execution and ownership. - Operate with high judgment and influence: Make clear tradeoffs under ambiguity, communicate decisions crisply across stakeholders, and drive outcomes through partnership rather than formal authority. You might thrive in this role if you - Bring 8+ years of engineering experience, including 2+ years managing high-performance engineers - Are deeply customer-obsessed and can partner credibly with senior stakeholders while keeping a high bar for delivery and technical rigor. - Naturally act as a shepherd: you elevate and refine others’ ideas, sharpen hypotheses, and make disciplined “scale vs pause” calls with clear reasoning. - Excel at cross-functional execution, forming tight partnerships with engineering, product, research, and GTM teams to deliver outcomes without needing formal authority. - Can build inclusive team mechanics – rotations, mentorship, and scoped ownership – that increase collaboration across teams rather than creating a gated platform group.
